title: Best Songwriters for Hire (2026): How to Hire One Online
description: How to hire a songwriter online: lyrics, melody or both, what to include, rights and credits, price factors and red flags.
intro: A songwriter can write lyrics, a melody, or a complete song for you to record, release or give as a gift. Collaborations work well when the brief is personal and specific, and the rights are settled in writing. They go wrong when ownership and credits are left vague, or when the song borrows too heavily from existing songs. This guide helps you commission a song that is truly yours.

faq.q: Can I hire someone to write lyrics only?
faq.a: Yes. You can order lyrics only, a melody only, or both. Say which you need, and whether you will write any part yourself.
It depends on the agreement. Some writers transfer all rights; others keep a credit or share of royalties. Agree on ownership, credits and any royalty split in writing before work starts.
Many songwriters include a simple demo with guitar, piano or a vocal guide. Ask whether a demo is included and what it will sound like.

faq.q: How personal can a song be?
faq.a: Very. For gifts or personal songs, share names, stories and details. The more specific you are, the more unique the song.

faq.q: How do I avoid a song that sounds like another?
faq.a: Ask the songwriter to confirm the melody and lyrics are original. If you share reference songs, explain you want the feel, not a copy.
